audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows contradicted their own why. win[1] said K'Sante while whys[1] ends 'neither gets a kill threat, so it stays even'; win[3] and win[4] said Skill while whys[3] calls it 'your tank lane-control peak' and whys[4] says All Out out-DPSes him; win[5] and win[6] said K'Sante while whys[5] says 'first items even it back out' and whys[6] says 'two armor-stackers stalemate'.
audit.why: 50.98% over 512 games — a genuinely even lane with a K'Sante mid-game bump. The packet chart (Skill, Skill, K'Sante, K'Sante, K'Sante, Skill, Skill) matches the prose line for line.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 set to Skill, K'Sante, K'Sante, Skill, Skill in phases[].side and win[] together. Existing 5/10-6/10 ratings already fit the corrected sides and were left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that no Maokai ability is ever named, and the page tells you to 'trade on his Q-knockback cooldown' without saying what that cooldown is.
audit.why: Bramble Smash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s — short enough that 'trade around it' means trading in a five-second window, which the reader needs the number to judge. Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s and Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s.
audit.corrected: Bramble Smash's 7s and Twisted Advance's 14/13/12/11/10s written into whys[3], mid, spikes[2], dosFull[0].d and the interactions row, with the names attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors, two of them reversing the actual mechanics. (1) 'W-charge unstoppable through his root' / 'your charged W is unstoppable and eats his root' — Riot's Path Maker text says reduced damage taken, never unstoppable; and Bramble Smash GROUNDS, so Maokai can shut the W, E and R dashes off entirely. The page told the reader the exact opposite of the truth. (2) Twisted Advance goes UNTARGETABLE during the dash — never mentioned, so the page's advice to hold W 'until he commits' walks you into spending everything on a target that cannot be hit. (3) 'Q3 knocks him up' in four paths — Ntofo Strikes has no knockup or third cast; at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls.
audit.why: Kit text is the authority, and both the grounding and the untargetable window flip decisions the reader makes every trade.
audit.corrected: Grounding and the untargetable dash written into spikes[2], early, the interactions row and wants.foe[0]; W re-described as a damage-reduced charge; the pull named correctly throughout.

The thing to respect is his W: it's a targeted root-dash, and if it lands while you're mid Q-combo he pins you for his Q-knockback plus a sapling free-hit. The thing to respect is his W: it goes untargetable mid-dash and roots on arrival, so anything you spend into it is wasted, and then Bramble Smash plus a sapling free-hit you. edits.before: Levels 3-5 are your window. With the full Q-W-Q3 combo you out-trade him: W through his W-root, Q3 knocks him up, and he has zero dash to peel away the follow-up. At 6, All Out is your real edge — it converts your tank stats into duelist damage that out-DPSes his passive sustain, and the recast yanks him out of position before his saplings reset. Trade on his Q-knockback cooldown, never into a sapling field.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are your window. With the full Q-W combo you out-trade him: charge W through his damage, land the two-stack Ntofo pull, and his W is a 14s cooldown he cannot re-dash on. Trade on Bramble Smash's 7s cooldown, never into a sapling field.
